records.title: Hetzner
records.text: Hetzner. Provision the control-plane VM on a Hetzner Cloud x86 server with OpenTofu, behind a Cloudflare Tunnel, with a data volume for Postgres and object storage.

records.title: Hetzner
records.text:
Provision a Hetzner Cloud server for the control plane with `infra/cp-hetzner`. Web traffic comes
through a Cloudflare Tunnel, and the firewall allows only SSH. Read
[OpenTofu per cloud](/self-host/terraform) first.

 
 This stack is also the one the hosted service runs on. It imports the hosted service's own DNS
 record (`dns-imports.tf`) and carries its email routing, switched off. Remove `dns-imports.tf`
 before you apply it to your zone, or the plan fails.

records.title: Hetzner
records.heading: What it creates
records.text:
- A `cx33` server (x86, 4 vCPU, 8 GB) and a 25 GB volume. Docker's data, so Postgres and the object
 store, live on the volume.
- Delete and rebuild protection on the server and the volume, and `prevent_destroy` in OpenTofu.
- A firewall that allows only SSH (port 22).
- The Cloudflare Tunnel, and proxied CNAME records for the apex and `www`.

At Hetzner's list price this costs about €14 a month: the server €13.10 and the volume €1.19.

records.title: Hetzner
records.heading: Before you begin
records.text:
- A Hetzner Cloud project and an API token for it.
- An SSH public key. SSH is the admin channel on Hetzner.
- The Cloudflare token, zone ID and account ID.

records.title: Hetzner
records.heading: Apply
records.text:
cd infra/cp-hetzner
cp backend.hcl.example backend.hcl
cp terraform.tfvars.example terraform.tfvars # hcloud_token, cloudflare_*, ssh_public_key, domain
tofu init -backend-config=backend.hcl
tofu plan -out=tfplan
tofu apply tfplan

Variables you may change: `server_type` (`cx43` for a busier instance), `data_volume_size`,
`location` (default `fsn1`), `ssh_allowed_cidrs`.

To remove the server later, first apply a change that turns the protections off, then destroy. See
`infra/cp-hetzner/README.md`.

records.title: Hetzner
records.heading: Check that it worked
records.text: ssh root@ ls /opt/alethia

records.title: Hetzner
records.heading: Related
records.text: - [OpenTofu per cloud](/self-host/terraform)

records.title: OpenTofu per cloud
records.text: OpenTofu per cloud. Provision a hardened control-plane VM and a Cloudflare Tunnel on Hetzner, AWS, GCP or Azure with OpenTofu, with no open web ports.

records.title: OpenTofu per cloud
records.text:
Provision the VM for a self-hosted instance as code. Each cloud has an OpenTofu stack in
`infra/cp- /` that creates one x86 VM with no open web port, and a Cloudflare Tunnel that
carries its traffic.

 
 These stacks prepare the VM: Docker, a clone of the repository in `/opt/alethia`, and the tunnel.
 They do not start Alethia, and the self-host bundle does not include the tunnel's connector
 (`cloudflared`). Use them only if you will run `cloudflared` on the VM yourself. Otherwise use the
 [installer](/self-host/install) or the [one-click templates](/self-host/one-click), which serve
 HTTPS directly.

records.title: OpenTofu per cloud
records.heading: Choose a cloud
records.text:
Apply one stack per domain. Two stacks on the same domain fight over its DNS records and tunnel.

 Cloud Stack Default VM Admin access Page 
 --- --- --- --- --- 
 Hetzner `infra/cp-hetzner` `cx33`, 4 vCPU, 8 GB SSH with a key [Hetzner](/self-host/terraform/hetzner) 
 AWS `infra/cp-aws` `t3.large`, 2 vCPU, 8 GB SSM Session Manager [AWS](/self-host/terraform/aws) 
 GCP `infra/cp-gcp` `e2-standard-2`, 2 vCPU, 8 GB SSH through IAP [GCP](/self-host/terraform/gcp) 
 Azure `infra/cp-azure` `Standard_D2s_v5`, 2 vCPU, 8 GB `az vm run-command` and Serial Console [Azure](/self-host/terraform/azure) 

Every VM is x86, because the images are `linux/amd64` only.

records.title: OpenTofu per cloud
records.heading: What every stack does
records.text:
- **No inbound web traffic.** The firewall opens no port 80 or 443. `cloudflared` on the VM dials out
 to Cloudflare, and TLS ends at Cloudflare's edge.
- **Proxied DNS.** The apex and `www` are proxied CNAME records onto ` .cfargotunnel.com`.
 The tunnel sends both to `http://caddy:80` on the VM.
- **Checks in the plan.** Each stack's `checks.tf` fails the plan if the posture regresses, for
 example if a web port opens.

records.title: OpenTofu per cloud
records.heading: Before you begin
records.text:
- A Cloudflare zone, its zone ID and account ID, and an API token with DNS edit and Cloudflare Tunnel
 permissions.
- An S3-compatible bucket for OpenTofu state.
- Credentials for the cloud. Use short-lived ones, such as the cloud CLI's sign-in.
- OpenTofu.

records.title: OpenTofu per cloud
records.heading: Apply a stack
records.text:
cd infra/cp- 
cp backend.hcl.example backend.hcl # the state bucket's endpoint and credentials
cp terraform.tfvars.example terraform.tfvars # domain, cloudflare_* IDs, cloud settings
tofu init -backend-config=backend.hcl
tofu plan -out=tfplan
tofu apply tfplan

Read the plan before you apply it. Then get the tunnel's token, which `cloudflared` needs:

tofu output -raw tunnel_token

The token is a secret. Pass it to `cloudflared` as `TUNNEL_TOKEN`; do not print it into logs.

records.title: OpenTofu per cloud
records.heading: Check that it worked
records.text:
The cloud console shows one VM named `alethia-cp`. In Cloudflare, the tunnel exists and the apex
record points at it. The tunnel shows as healthy once `cloudflared` runs on the VM.

records.title: OpenTofu per cloud
records.heading: Related
records.text:
- [Install on a VM](/self-host/install): start the bundle on the VM.
- [Configuration](/self-host/configuration#domain-and-client-ip): how the console reads the client
 IP address, which a tunnel changes.

records.title: Upgrade and back up
records.text: Upgrade and back up. Back up a self-hosted Alethia bundle, upgrade it to a new image tag, and restore it from a backup.

records.title: Upgrade and back up
records.text:
Back up the three things that hold state, then upgrade by running the installer again. To roll back,
restore the backup: never run an older image against a newer database schema.

The commands on this page run on the VM, from `/opt/alethia`. Define this shortcut first:

cd /opt/alethia
alias dc='docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f deploy/selfhost/docker-compose.selfhost.yml'

records.title: Upgrade and back up
records.heading: What to back up
records.text:
What Why it matters 
 --- --- 
 `.env` Holds the instance secrets. Without `ALETHIA_CRED_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, stored connector secrets cannot be decrypted. Keep this copy somewhere encrypted. 
 Postgres Every project, environment, job and user. 
 The `alethia_seaweedfs-data` volume OpenTofu state and plan files. State cannot be rebuilt, and without it Alethia cannot change or destroy what it created.

records.title: Upgrade and back up
records.heading: Dump the database
records.text:
dc exec -T postgres pg_dump -U alethia -d alethia -Fc > alethia-$(date +%F).dump

Run it from cron every day. It does not stop the console.

records.title: Upgrade and back up
records.heading: Copy the object store
records.text:
Stop the store for a consistent copy, then start it again:

dc stop seaweedfs
docker run --rm -v alethia_seaweedfs-data:/data -v "$PWD":/backup alpine \
 tar czf /backup/seaweedfs-$(date +%F).tgz -C /data .
dc start seaweedfs

records.title: Upgrade and back up
records.heading: Move the copies off the VM
records.text:
Copy `.env`, the dump and the archive to storage outside the VM, such as a bucket in another
account. A cloud snapshot of the VM's disk (EBS snapshots, Hetzner backups) is a second copy, not a
replacement: it restores the whole VM, not one table.

records.title: Upgrade and back up
records.heading: Upgrade
records.text:
1. Take a backup.
2. Run the installer again, with the tag you want:

 curl -fsSL https://get.alethialabs.io/self-host ALETHIA_VERSION= sh
 
 Without `ALETHIA_VERSION`, it keeps the tag recorded in `.env`. With `latest`, each run pulls
 the newest build.

The installer updates the compose files in `/opt/alethia`, adds any new instance secret to `.env`,
and keeps every value already there. The `migrate` service applies the new schema before `app`
starts. Move one minor version at a time.

records.title: Upgrade and back up
records.heading: Check that it worked
records.text:
dc ps

`migrate` has exited with code 0, and `app` is `running`. If `migrate` failed, read
`dc logs migrate`, then restore the backup.

records.title: Upgrade and back up
records.heading: Restore
records.text:
dc stop app runner
dc exec -T postgres pg_restore -U alethia -d alethia --clean --if-exists < alethia- .dump
dc stop seaweedfs
docker run --rm -v alethia_seaweedfs-data:/data -v "$PWD":/backup alpine \
 sh -c 'rm -rf /data/* && tar xzf /backup/seaweedfs- .tgz -C /data'
dc up -d

Restore the `.env` from the same backup first, and set `ALETHIA_VERSION` in it to the tag the backup
was taken on.

records.title: Upgrade and back up
records.heading: Inspect the database
records.text:
dc --profile tools up -d pgweb

pgweb listens on port 8081 of the VM. Reach it through an SSH tunnel; do not open the port.

records.title: Upgrade and back up
records.heading: Related
records.text:
- [Configuration](/self-host/configuration): rotate instance secrets.
- [Changelog](/changelog): breaking changes and upgrade steps.

records.title: Billing and plans
records.text: Billing and plans. Fix a plan or trial that cannot start, a failed payment, and refusals from plan and usage limits.

records.title: Billing and plans
records.text:
Manage plans on the **Billing** page in the console's settings. Prices are on the
[pricing page](https://alethialabs.io/pricing), and each plan's ceilings are in
[Limits](/reference/limits).

records.title: Billing and plans
records.heading: "Alethia is not yet able to sell to customers in this country in this capacity."
records.text:
**Cause:** paid plans open one market at a time, and are not open yet for your country or for the way
you buy (as an individual or for an organization). The pricing page shows which markets are open.

**Fix:** keep using the Hobby plan. It stays free, with no time limit. To hear when your market
opens, write to sales@alethialabs.io.

An organization in an EU country other than Bulgaria that has a VAT number can't be charged yet.
Alethia can give such an organization complimentary Early Access instead: the paid plan with nothing
charged and nothing owed. Billing starts only after the organization agrees to pay, and the free
period is never charged. To ask for it, write to sales@alethialabs.io.

records.title: Billing and plans
records.heading: A purchase asks for more information first
records.text:
The console shows one of these before it starts a purchase:

 Message What to do 
 --- --- 
 "Accept the current Terms of Service before subscribing." Accept the terms when the console asks, then try again. 
 "Tell us whether you are buying as an individual or on behalf of an organization …" Choose one. The two carry different rights. 
 "Add a billing address before subscribing." Add the address on the **Billing** page.

records.title: Billing and plans
records.heading: "Couldn't start the purchase. Billing may not be configured on this deployment"
records.text:
**Cause:** the console could not start the payment. On a self-hosted console, billing is often not
set up at all.

**Fix:** try again. If it continues on alethialabs.io, open a support case from **Support** in the
sidebar.

records.title: Billing and plans
records.heading: The Pro trial is not offered, or is refused
records.text:
Message Cause 
 --- --- 
 "This organization has already used its free Pro trial. …" Each organization gets one trial. 
 "Your account has already used its free Pro trial. …" Each person gets one trial, across every organization. 
 "Too many Pro trials have been started from your network recently, so a new one can't start now. …" Your network reached the trial ceiling in [Limits](/reference/limits). 

**Fix:** you can still subscribe to Pro from the **Billing** page, when paid plans are open for you.

records.title: Billing and plans
records.heading: The trial ended
records.text:
**Cause:** the Pro trial lasts 30 days and needs no card. When it ends without a paid plan, the
organization goes back to the Hobby plan. Alethia sends an email when this happens.

**Fix:** nothing is deleted. Projects, environments, and clusters stay, and the Hobby plan's limits
apply again. To keep Pro, subscribe on the **Billing** page.

records.title: Billing and plans
records.heading: "Payment failed"
records.text:
The **Billing** page shows **Payment failed**: "The last payment for … didn't go through, so this
organization's paid features are paused until a payment succeeds." Alethia also sends an email.

**Cause:** the card was declined, expired, or needs your bank's confirmation.

**Fix:** select **Update the payment method**. If you see "Ask a member with the billing permission
to update the payment method.", ask a member who manages billing.

records.title: Billing and plans
records.heading: "The payment did not complete — the card may have been declined, or your bank may need you to confirm it."
records.text:
**Cause:** the payment for a new organization's plan did not complete. The organization is on the
Hobby plan until it is paid.

**Fix:** confirm the payment with your bank, or try another card. If the console says the payment is
still being confirmed, wait. A bank debit can take several business days.

records.title: Billing and plans
records.heading: A feature says it needs another plan
records.text:
**Cause:** the feature is part of a higher plan. The dialog says which one: "This feature is
available on the … plan."

**Fix:** upgrade on the **Billing** page, or compare plans on the
[pricing page](https://alethialabs.io/pricing).

records.title: Billing and plans
records.heading: Job and minute limits
records.text:
The daily job limit and the monthly provisioning minutes are described in
[Troubleshoot a deploy](/troubleshooting/deploy#the-daily-job-limit-is-reached).

records.title: Cluster access
records.text: Cluster access. Fix a kubeconfig that the CLI or the console will not give you, and a kubectl that says Unauthorized.

records.title: Cluster access
records.text:
Find the message you see, then do what the row says. `alethia cluster kubeconfig` prints errors
after `Error:`. `alethia cluster token` prints them after `alethia cluster token:`, and `kubectl`
shows that line. How cluster access works is in [Cluster access](/concepts/cluster-access).

records.title: Cluster access
records.heading: kubectl says "You must be logged in to the server (Unauthorized)"
records.text:
**Cause:** the credential expired, or someone revoked it.

**Fix:** with a static kubeconfig, run `alethia cluster kubeconfig` again. With an exec kubeconfig,
the cache may still hold a revoked token, for example after someone deleted the `alethia-view`
ServiceAccount. Delete the cache directory (see
[the cache locations](/concepts/cluster-access#exec-and-static-kubeconfigs)), then run `kubectl`
again.

records.title: Cluster access
records.heading: The control plane refuses the request
records.text:
Status Message Fix 
 --- --- --- 
 401 your session is not valid — run `alethia login`, then try again Run `alethia login`. 
 402 your organization's plan does not allow another kubeconfig right now: … The mint uses runner minutes. Run `alethia usage` to see the limit you reached. 
 403 your role cannot mint a kubeconfig for this cluster (owners, admins and operators can) Ask an owner or admin for a role with `cluster:access_readonly`. 
 403 you cannot mint an admin kubeconfig for this cluster: … drop --admin for read-only access Run it without `--admin`. For admin access, sign in as yourself with `alethia login`, or ask for a role with `cluster:access_admin`. 
 404 the cluster was not found in the active organization Run `alethia org switch`, or pass `--org`. 
 409 The cluster has not been provisioned, so there is nothing to mint a kubeconfig for Deploy the environment. Drafts and environments being destroyed cannot get a kubeconfig. 
 422 This cluster's cloud cannot mint a kubeconfig through Alethia The cluster is not on AWS, GCP, Azure or Hetzner. Use the cloud's own CLI. 
 429 too many kubeconfig requests — try again in … You made more than 20 requests in 10 minutes in this org

records.title: Cluster access
records.heading: The CLI gives up while it waits
records.text:
Message Fix 
 --- --- 
 the kubeconfig request expired before a runner completed it … No runner took the job within 10 minutes. Check `alethia runner list`. 
 timed out waiting for a runner to mint the kubeconfig … The same, measured on your clock. Check `alethia runner list`. 
 the kubeconfig request is gone (already collected, or expired and swept) Run the command again. A credential can be collected only once. 
 your role no longer allows collecting this kubeconfig Your role changed during the mint. Ask for the permission again. 
 the minted credential had already expired when it arrived … Set your machine's clock correctly.

records.title: Cluster access
records.heading: The runner could not mint the kubeconfig
records.text:
The CLI prints `the runner could not mint the kubeconfig:` and one of these reasons.

 Reason Fix 
 --- --- 
 The runner could not mint the credential. Read the job log: `alethia jobs logs --latest --type MINT_KUBECONFIG`. 
 The cluster was not found in the cloud account. The cluster was deleted or renamed outside Alethia. Check the cloud console. 
 The runner could not reach the cluster's API endpoint. Check that the runner's network can reach the endpoint. 
 The runner could not assume the cluster's cloud identity. Check the connection in [Connectors](/guides/connectors). 
 The cloud refused to issue a credential for this cluster. Give the cloud identity permission to get cluster credentials. 
 The read-only identity could not be prepared in the cluster. Check whether someone changed the `alethia-view` ServiceAccount or the `alethia:view` ClusterRole. 
 This cloud cannot issue the requested kubeconfig shape. Run it again with or without `--static`. 
 The runner could not seal the credential to the client key. Run the command again. 
 Kubeconfig mints are not available for an environment placed on a shared cluster. The environment uses a `namespace` or `vcluster` placement. Only `

records.title: Cluster access
records.heading: The CLI rejects the command
records.text:
Message Fix 
 --- --- 
 --ttl must be whole seconds from 15m to 8h Pass a TTL from `15m` to `8h`. 
 --output takes a file path here (or - for stdout), not a format `--output` takes a file name. For a file called `json`, pass `./json`. 
 if any flags in the group [merge output] are set none of the others can be Pass `--merge` or `--output`, not both. 
 … is locked by another writer (kubectl?) Another program is writing your kubeconfig. If nothing is, delete the `.lock` file the message names.

records.title: Cluster access
records.heading: The console download fails
records.text:
The console uses the same checks and the same rate limit as the CLI.

 Message Fix 
 --- --- 
 Your plan's usage limit is reached, so no new kubeconfig can be minted. Check your plan's usage. 
 You need cluster read-only access to download a kubeconfig. Ask an owner or admin for a role with `cluster:access_readonly`. 
 This cluster was not found. Reload the page. The cluster may have been removed. 
 This cluster has not finished provisioning, so there is no kubeconfig to mint yet. Deploy the environment, or wait for the deploy to finish. 
 This cluster's cloud cannot mint a kubeconfig through Alethia. Use the cloud's own CLI. 
 Too many kubeconfig requests. Try again in a few minutes. Wait. Your CLI and console requests count together. 
 No runner finished the kubeconfig in time. … Check that a runner is online, then try again. 
 Still waiting for a runner to mint it. Shown after 20 seconds. Check the runners, or select **Cancel**. 
 This browser cannot create the X25519 key the download is sealed to. … Use Chrome 133, Firefox 130, Safari 17 or later, or the CLI. 
 Downloading a kubeconfig in the browser needs HTTPS … Open the console over HTTPS, or use the CLI. 
 The kubeconfig co

records.title: Connect a cloud
records.text: Connect a cloud. Fix a cloud connection that fails to verify, or verifies with limited permissions, on AWS, GCP, Azure, or Hetzner.

records.title: Connect a cloud
records.text:
When you select **Connect** on a setup sheet, the console checks the connection at once. No runner
is involved. The result is one of three states:

- **Connected**: Alethia can sign in and has the permissions it checks for.
- **Limited permissions**: Alethia can sign in, but some permissions are missing. The connector
 lists them.
- **Verification failed**: Alethia cannot sign in. The account shows the reason.

To read the reason, open **Connectors**, select **Manage** on the card, and open the account. After
you fix the cause, select **Re-verify**. See
[Re-verify a connection](/guides/connectors/managing-connections#re-verify-a-connection).

From the CLI, a failed check prints `connection test failed` with the reason, and exits with code 13.
The [connector commands](/reference/cli/connector#troubleshooting) have their own table of messages.

records.title: Connect a cloud
records.heading: "aws CLI not found on PATH", "gcloud CLI not found on PATH", or "az CLI not found on PATH"
records.text:
**Cause:** `alethia connector aws`, `gcp`, or `azure` runs the cloud's own CLI on your machine, and
it is not installed.

**Fix:** install the cloud's CLI and sign in to it. Or run the setup in the cloud's browser shell
from the console instead. For GCP, "gcloud is not authenticated" means you need to run
`gcloud auth login` first.

records.title: Connect a cloud
records.heading: "… is not available in this release."
records.text:
**Cause:** that cloud is not offered by this console.

**Fix:** use AWS, GCP, Azure, or Hetzner.

records.title: Connect a cloud
records.heading: Verification failed after the role ARN is pasted
records.text:
**Cause:** AWS refused to let Alethia assume the role. The reason AWS gives is shown as it is.
Common causes are a role that was deleted, or a trust policy that does not name Alethia's issuer.

**Fix:** run the setup command again in AWS CloudShell. It reuses the IAM OIDC identity provider if
one exists. Then paste the new role ARN. An AWS account can have only one IAM OIDC identity provider
for each issuer URL. See [AWS verification](/guides/connectors/aws#verification).

records.title: Connect a cloud
records.heading: "Invalid format. Expected: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/RoleName"
records.text:
**Cause:** the value in **IAM Role ARN** is not a role ARN.

**Fix:** copy the role ARN that the setup script prints. You can paste the whole output, and the
field keeps only the ARN.

records.title: Connect a cloud
records.heading: Limited permissions, with ec2:DescribeRegions or ec2:DescribeVpcs listed
records.text:
**Cause:** the role can be assumed, but it cannot run those read calls.

**Fix:** add the permissions in [IAM role permissions](/guides/connectors/aws#iam-role-permissions)
to the role, then select **Re-verify**.

records.title: Connect a cloud
records.heading: "cloudformation deploy failed" or "stack did not produce a RoleArn output"
records.text:
**Cause:** `alethia connector aws` could not create the `AlethiaConnect` stack. The AWS message
follows.

**Fix:** check that the `aws` CLI is signed in to the right account, and that you can create IAM
roles there. Then run the command again.

records.title: Connect a cloud
records.heading: "GCP authentication failed"
records.text:
**Cause:** Alethia could not exchange its token through your Workload Identity Pool. The pool, its
provider, or the service account binding is missing or different from what the setup created.

**Fix:** run the setup command again in Cloud Shell, then select **Re-verify**. See
[GCP verification](/guides/connectors/gcp#verification).

records.title: Connect a cloud
records.heading: "Access to project … was denied"
records.text:
**Cause:** the service account that Alethia uses has no access to the project.

**Fix:** check that **Project ID** and **Project number** name the project where you ran the setup.
Then run the setup again.

records.title: Connect a cloud
records.heading: Limited permissions, with "(API not enabled)" next to an API
records.text:
**Cause:** a Google Cloud API that provisioning needs is turned off in the project.

**Fix:** turn on the API with `gcloud services enable`, then select **Re-verify**. See
[Optional APIs you enable yourself](/guides/connectors/gcp#optional-apis-you-enable-yourself).

records.title: Connect a cloud
records.heading: "This GCP connection uses the retired AWS-hub setup."
records.text:
**Cause:** the connection was made with an older setup that Alethia no longer supports.

**Fix:** connect GCP again from **Connectors**.

records.title: Connect a cloud
records.heading: "Project number must be digits only."
records.text:
**Cause:** **Project number** contains something other than digits.

**Fix:** paste the project number that the setup script prints. It is not the project ID.

records.title: Connect a cloud
records.heading: "No application with that Client ID exists in tenant …"
records.text:
**Cause:** **Client ID** does not name the managed identity. A subscription ID in this field is the
usual mistake.

**Fix:** paste the managed identity's client ID. To print it, run
`az identity show --query clientId`.

records.title: Connect a cloud
records.heading: "Tenant … was not found."
records.text:
**Cause:** **Tenant ID** is wrong.

**Fix:** paste the tenant ID. To print it, run `az account show --query tenantId`.

records.title: Connect a cloud
records.heading: "The managed identity has no federated credential matching this console's OIDC issuer."
records.text:
**Cause:** the managed identity does not trust this console. On a self-hosted console, this also
happens after the console's URL changes.

**Fix:** run the setup command again. It is safe to run more than once. Then select **Re-verify**.

records.title: Connect a cloud
records.heading: "Access to subscription … was denied"
records.text:
**Cause:** the managed identity has no role on the subscription.

**Fix:** assign the role that the setup assigns. See
[Assign the least-privilege role](/guides/connectors/azure#assign-the-least-privilege-role).

records.title: Connect a cloud
records.heading: "Invalid Tenant ID format. Expected a UUID."
records.text:
**Cause:** an ID field does not contain a UUID. The same message exists for **Client ID** and
**Subscription ID**.

**Fix:** paste the IDs that the setup script prints. To fill both ID fields at once, select
**Paste all** and paste the whole output.

records.title: Connect a cloud
records.heading: "Token rejected by hetzner"
records.text:
**Cause:** the token is wrong, was deleted, or has only **Read** permission.

**Fix:** create a new token with **Read & Write** permission in the Hetzner Cloud Console, and
paste it. See [Hetzner verification](/guides/connectors/hetzner#verification).

records.title: Connect a cloud
records.heading: "Invalid API token format"
records.text:
**Cause:** the value is too short to be a Hetzner Cloud API token. It was probably cut off when you
copied it.

**Fix:** copy the whole token again. The Hetzner Cloud Console shows a token only once, so create a
new one if you no longer have it.

records.title: Connect a cloud
records.heading: "the token contains whitespace — copy it without line breaks"
records.text:
**Cause:** `alethia connector hetzner` found a space or a line break in the token.

**Fix:** copy the token again as one line.

records.title: Connect a cloud
records.heading: "no token given: pass --token, or pipe it with --token-stdin"
records.text:
**Cause:** `alethia connector hetzner` ran without a terminal, so it cannot ask for the token.

**Fix:** pipe the token in, for example `alethia connector hetzner --no-input --token-stdin < token.txt`.

records.title: Connect a cloud
records.heading: "Provide both the Hetzner S3 access key and secret key, or neither."
records.text:
**Cause:** only one of the two Object Storage keys was entered.

**Fix:** enter both keys, or leave both empty.

records.title: Deploy
records.text: Deploy. Fix a deploy that waits for a runner, is blocked by the verify gate, is refused by a plan limit, or fails in the job log.

records.title: Deploy
records.text:
A runner claims a deploy job, plans with OpenTofu, runs the
[verify gate](/guides/jobs/plan-and-apply#verify-gate), and applies. Start with the job log: open the
job from **Jobs**, select **View log** on the canvas, or run `alethia jobs logs --latest --follow`.

records.title: Deploy
records.heading: The job waits for a runner
records.text:
The job page shows **Waiting for a runner**. After two minutes it shows **Still waiting for a
runner** and a **View runners** button.

**Cause:** no runner has claimed the job. A job stays queued until one does. The usual reasons:

- No runner that can take the job is online.
- The runner you selected does not take jobs for this cloud.
- Your plan's limit on jobs that run at the same time is reached. Extra jobs wait. They are not
 refused. See [Free plan limits](/guides/jobs/plan-and-apply#free-plan-limits).
- Another job on the same environment is still running. Jobs on one environment run one at a time.

**Fix:** select **View runners** and check that a runner is online. If other jobs are running, wait
for them to finish. To register your own runner, see [Runners](/guides/runners).

From the CLI, `alethia apply` refuses a runner that does not take the project's cloud. The message
says `does not take … jobs`. Run `alethia runner list`, and name a runner that does with `--runner`.

records.title: Deploy
records.heading: "No runner is registered to run this job."
records.text:
**Cause:** the organization has no runner to select, so **Confirm** is turned off.

**Fix:** select **Register a runner**, or see [Runners](/guides/runners).

records.title: Deploy
records.heading: The daily job limit is reached
records.text:
The console says "The Hobby plan allows … provisioning jobs per day. You've hit the limit — it
clears over the next 24 hours, or upgrade to remove it."

**Cause:** a Hobby organization started the most provisioning jobs it can start in 24 hours. Plans,
deploys, destroys, and scans that you start count. Kubeconfig requests and jobs that the platform
runs for you do not. The current number is in [Limits](/reference/limits).

**Fix:** wait until older jobs leave the 24-hour window, or upgrade the organization.

records.title: Deploy
records.heading: The monthly provisioning minutes are used up
records.text:
The console says "You've used your … included provisioning minutes this month. Upgrade to keep
provisioning."

**Cause:** on the Hobby plan, runner time counts against the minutes the plan includes each month.

**Fix:** upgrade the organization, or wait for the next month. On a paid plan with a usage cap, the
message is "Usage cap reached" instead: raise or turn off the cap on the **Billing** page.

records.title: Deploy
records.heading: "verification gate BLOCKED apply: failing controls …"
records.text:
**Cause:** the plan failed one or more controls of the verify gate, so the runner stopped before it
changed anything. The message lists the failing controls.

**Fix:** change the design so that the controls pass, then run the plan and deploy again. If your
organization accepts the risk, someone with the right permission can record an override on the
queued deploy. See [Verify override](/guides/jobs/verify-override).

A message that starts with "verification gate produced no verdict" means the gate could not
evaluate the plan at all. The runner refuses to apply in that case too. Read the cause in the
message.

records.title: Deploy
records.heading: "compatibility gate (…) BLOCKED apply"
records.text:
**Cause:** the Kubernetes minor version and an add-on version in the design do not work together.

**Fix:** change the Kubernetes version or the add-on version, then plan and deploy again.

records.title: Deploy
records.heading: "configuration changed since plan was generated"
records.text:
**Cause:** the design changed after the plan was made. A deploy applies only the plan that was
reviewed.

**Fix:** run the plan again, read it, and deploy.

records.title: Deploy
records.heading: "plan job … has status …, expected SUCCESS"
records.text:
**Cause:** the deploy is bound to a plan that did not succeed.

**Fix:** fix what the plan job's log reports, then run the plan again.

records.title: Deploy
records.heading: "failed to assume role …"
records.text:
**Cause:** the runner could not sign in to your AWS account with the connected role.

**Fix:** open **Connectors** and select **Re-verify** on the account. If verification fails, see
[Troubleshoot connecting a cloud](/troubleshooting/connect#aws).

records.title: Deploy
records.heading: A runner stopped during the job
records.text:
**Cause:** the runner crashed or lost its connection while it held the job.

**Fix:** nothing, at first. Alethia puts the job back in the queue, and another runner continues it.
OpenTofu state is kept, so the next attempt starts from what was already applied. After several
failed attempts the job fails. See [Failure recovery](/concepts/job-queue#failure-recovery).

records.title: Deploy
records.heading: CLI exit codes while waiting
records.text:
Message Exit code What to do 
 --- --- --- 
 `job failed: …` 13 Read the log with `alethia jobs logs `. 
 `job was cancelled` 13 Start the deploy again if the cancel was a mistake. 
 `timed out after … waiting for job …; it is still running` 12 The job continues. Follow it with `alethia jobs logs --follow`. 

For every exit code of `alethia apply`, see
[Exit codes of `apply`](/reference/cli/plan-and-apply#exit-codes-of-apply).

records.title: Design and GitOps
records.text: Design and GitOps. Fix problems with a design on the canvas, a plan that fails on a design value, and an ArgoCD sync after a deploy.

records.title: Design and GitOps
records.text:
Find the problem you see, then do what the block says. How to design each resource is in
[Design a project](/guides/design-project).

records.title: Design and GitOps
records.heading: A card is gated
records.text:
**Symptom:** a card has a faint dot and reads **Gated**.

**Cause:** a core resource (network, cluster or a data service) is placed on a different cloud from
the project. It is drawn but will not provision.

**Fix:** place the resource on the project's cloud account.

records.title: Design and GitOps
records.heading: A card reads Needs setup on a live resource
records.text:
**Symptom:** a deployed resource shows a hollow ring and **Needs setup**.

**Cause:** its design has a value that would fail the next deploy, such as an empty required field.

**Fix:** open the card. The group with the problem is open, and the problem shows under the field.

records.title: Design and GitOps
records.heading: The CIDR block is refused
records.text:
**Symptom:** the network's **CIDR block** says the cloud needs a wider block.

**Cause:** AWS and Azure need a `/18` or wider, and Hetzner a `/22` or wider, to carve subnets.

**Fix:** use a wider block, such as `10.0.0.0/16`.

records.title: Design and GitOps
records.heading: A Hetzner deploy fails on the Kubernetes version
records.text:
**Symptom:** the deploy fails with an error that names Kubernetes 1.35.6.

**Cause:** the cluster has another version set, for example from the CLI. Talos installs one pinned
version.

**Fix:** clear the cluster's version, or set it to `1.35`.

records.title: Design and GitOps
records.heading: A GCP deploy is refused for the instance type
records.text:
**Symptom:** a deploy onto `e2-medium` or `n1-standard-1` is refused before it starts.

**Cause:** GKE reserves most of those machines' CPU, so the cluster add-ons cannot run.

**Fix:** choose `e2-standard-2` or larger.

records.title: Design and GitOps
records.heading: A node pool key is not a variable of this template
records.text:
**Symptom:** writing `node_labels`, `node_taints` or `extra_node_pools` fails with
`not a variable of this template`.

**Cause:** the cloud's template does not accept the key.

**Fix:** remove the key. The [node pools reference](/reference/node-pools) lists which clouds accept
each key. A plan error that names a rule means a value breaks that rule: fix the value.

records.title: Design and GitOps
records.heading: IAM authentication is unavailable
records.text:
**Symptom:** the database's **IAM authentication** switch is disabled, or a deploy fails with
"Unavailable on Hetzner".

**Cause:** Hetzner runs PostgreSQL in your cluster, with no cloud identity to mint tokens. A
database moved there keeps its setting, and Alethia refuses to fall back to a password.

**Fix:** turn **IAM authentication** off to use a generated password, or move the database to AWS,
GCP or Azure.

records.title: Design and GitOps
records.heading: A keyless binding is omitted at deploy
records.text:
**Symptom:** the **Deploy** tab says a binding was omitted, or the bootstrap Job was skipped.

**Cause:** Alethia could not wire the binding, for example because an identity is missing, or could
not resolve the Job's admin credential. It leaves them out rather than deploy a workload that points
at nothing.

**Fix:** read the reason on the **Deploy** tab. Check that the runner has
`ALETHIA_KEYLESS_DB_AUTH_ENABLED=true` and runs a published image, then deploy again.

records.title: Design and GitOps
records.heading: Azure refuses an ordered queue
records.text:
**Symptom:** a project with an ordered Service Bus queue is blocked before it deploys.

**Cause:** sessions need the Standard or Premium tier, and the queue's `service_bus_sku` is `Basic`.

**Fix:** set `service_bus_sku` to `Standard` (the default) or `Premium` in the queue's
`provider_config`, or turn off **Ordered (FIFO) delivery**.

records.title: Design and GitOps
records.heading: A public bucket is refused on GCP
records.text:
**Symptom:** the deploy refuses a bucket with **Public access** on.

**Cause:** the organization policy `constraints/iam.allowedPolicyMemberDomains` blocks public grants.

**Fix:** turn **Public access** off, or ask your GCP administrator for an exception.

records.title: Design and GitOps
records.heading: The deploy succeeded but the cluster is empty
records.text:
**Symptom:** ArgoCD's `apps` Application is synced, but none of your resources exist.

**Cause:** the synced directory holds no manifests. ArgoCD reads only the synced directory itself,
not its subdirectories, unless it is a Kustomize or Helm source.

**Fix:** put your manifests directly in the repository root, or in the overlay path; or add a
`kustomization.yaml` there.

records.title: Design and GitOps
records.heading: The addons Application shows a ComparisonError
records.text:
**Symptom:** after a successful deploy, ArgoCD shows the `addons` Application in red.

**Cause:** the repository has no `addons/` directory yet.

**Fix:** enable your first add-on in GitOps mode, or create an empty `addons/` directory.

records.title: Design and GitOps
records.heading: A manifest fails to sync because of its namespace
records.text:
**Symptom:** ArgoCD reports that a namespace does not exist.

**Cause:** ArgoCD does not create the namespaces your manifests name.

**Fix:** add a `Namespace` manifest to the same directory.

records.title: Design and GitOps
records.heading: The deploy fails because there is no Git access
records.text:
**Symptom:** the deploy fails and says to connect the Git provider or make the repository public.

**Cause:** the job owner has no token for the repository's host, and an anonymous `https://` probe
failed. An `ssh://` or `git@host:path` repository is never probed.

**Fix:** connect the [Git provider](/guides/connectors/git-providers) for the job owner, or make the
repository public.

records.title: Design and GitOps
records.heading: GitOps mode is refused
records.text:
**Symptom:** choosing GitOps mode for an add-on, or queuing a plan, is refused with a message to use
Managed delivery.

**Cause:** the apps repository is not on GitHub, or is on a host that matches no connected provider.
Only a GitHub connection can push.

**Fix:** use Managed delivery for those add-ons, or move the apps repository to GitHub.

records.title: Design and GitOps
records.heading: A chart is skipped because of its namespace
records.text:
**Symptom:** the **Deploy** tab warns that a bring-your-own chart was skipped, or moved.

**Cause:** the chart was attached in a namespace the platform reserves. A chart in `default` moves
to its own namespace. A chart in any other reserved namespace is skipped: its workloads from an
earlier deploy stay but stop syncing, and its binding secrets are removed.

**Fix:** attach the chart again with a namespace of your own.

records.title: Design and GitOps
records.heading: A bring-your-own IaC module cannot be attached or detached
records.text:
**Symptom:** attaching a module is rejected, or **✕** on the **External IaC** card is refused.

**Cause:** attaching needs an environment with no deployed or in-progress template infrastructure.
Detaching needs a module that has never deployed.

**Fix:** destroy the environment first, then attach or detach.

records.title: Design and GitOps
records.heading: A bring-your-own IaC deploy stays locked
records.text:
**Symptom:** the module's scan reads **Issues found — resolve before deploying**, and nothing
deploys.

**Cause:** a failed scan clears the deploy pin.

**Fix:** fix each `error` finding, push, and select **Rescan**.

records.title: Destroy
records.text: Destroy. Fix a destroy that is refused, fails, waits on a state lock, or leaves cloud load balancers behind.

records.title: Destroy
records.text:
A destroy is a job that removes an environment's cloud resources. In the console, start it from the
canvas: **More**, then **Environment settings**, then **Destroy** under **Danger zone**. From the
CLI, run `alethia project destroy`. See
[`alethia project destroy`](/reference/cli/plan-and-apply#alethia-project-destroy).

 
Until a destroy job succeeds, your cloud provider can still bill you for the environment's
resources. Check the job's result. Do not assume it finished.

records.title: Destroy
records.heading: Deleting is not destroying
records.text:
Deleting an environment record or a project removes it from Alethia. It destroys **nothing** in the
cloud. The console refuses to delete an environment or a project that is still live, with
"Destroy this environment before deleting it." or "This project has live or in-flight environments.
Destroy them before deleting the project."

**Fix:** destroy each environment first, then delete.

records.title: Destroy
records.heading: Other environments run on this environment's cluster
records.text:
The console asks you to destroy several environments at once, or the CLI refuses with a list of the
environments placed on this one.

**Cause:** other environments are placed on this environment's cluster. Destroying the cluster would
remove them too.

**Fix:** destroy those environments first. Or destroy them all together: in the console, type the
project name and confirm. In the CLI, add `--cascade`. See
[Destroying an environment that other environments run on](/reference/cli/plan-and-apply#destroying-an-environment-that-other-environments-run-on).

With `--cascade`, the first environment's destroy waits until the others are gone. If one of their
destroys fails, it keeps waiting. Destroy the failed environment again, or cancel the waiting job
with `alethia jobs cancel`.

records.title: Destroy
records.heading: "tofu destroy failed"
records.text:
**Cause:** OpenTofu could not remove one or more resources. The log shows the resource and the
cloud's reason.

**Fix:** fix the cause in the log, then run the destroy again. OpenTofu state is kept, so the next
destroy continues from what is left. See
[State and failure recovery](/concepts/terraform-state#state-and-failure-recovery).

records.title: Destroy
records.heading: Load balancers were not released
records.text:
The log says "CLOUD LOAD BALANCERS MAY STILL EXIST AND STILL BILL.", or the job fails with "the
environment's cloud resources were destroyed, but its load balancers were not released".

**Cause:** a Kubernetes service on the cluster created a load balancer in your cloud account, and the
destroy could not remove it. Nothing removes these automatically.

**Fix:** delete those services from the cluster and run the destroy again. Or delete the load
balancers in your cloud provider's console.

records.title: Destroy
records.heading: "namespace teardown … completed with errors — re-run the destroy to converge"
records.text:
**Cause:** some objects in a namespace could not be removed in one pass.

**Fix:** run the destroy again.

records.title: Destroy
records.heading: The destroy waits on a state lock
records.text:
The job does not start, or OpenTofu reports that the state is locked.

**Cause:** another job on the same environment holds the state lock. Jobs on one environment run one
at a time. A lock is released when its job ends, also when the job is cancelled or its runner
crashes.

**Fix:** wait for the other job to finish, or cancel it from its job page or with
`alethia jobs cancel`. Then run the destroy again.

records.title: Destroy
records.heading: The destroy was cancelled before it started
records.text:
The job page says "This job has not started — no runner has claimed it and nothing has been applied."

**Cause:** the job was cancelled while it waited in the queue. Nothing was changed.

**Fix:** start the destroy again. If it waits for a runner, see
[The job waits for a runner](/troubleshooting/deploy#the-job-waits-for-a-runner).

records.title: Destroy
records.heading: The daily job limit is reached
records.text:
A destroy you start is a provisioning job, so it counts toward the daily job limit on the Hobby plan.
See [The daily job limit is reached](/troubleshooting/deploy#the-daily-job-limit-is-reached).

records.title: Troubleshooting
records.text: Troubleshooting. Find the message you see, learn what causes it, and fix it — for sign-in, connecting a cloud, deploying, destroying, cluster access and billing.

records.title: Troubleshooting
records.text:
Each page lists problems by what you see: a console message, a CLI message, or a step that does not
finish. Messages are quoted as the product shows them, so search for the text you see.

 
 
 Sign-in codes, sign-up refusals, and `alethia login`.
 
 
 A connection that fails to verify, or has limited permissions.
 
 
 A job that waits for a runner, a blocked verify gate, and job limits.
 
 
 A destroy that is refused, fails, or leaves load balancers behind.
 
 
 A gated card, a design value a plan refuses, and an ArgoCD sync that delivers nothing.
 
 
 A kubeconfig you cannot get, and `kubectl` saying Unauthorized.
 
 
 Plans not open yet, trials, failed payments, and usage limits.

records.title: Troubleshooting
records.heading: First checks
records.text:
- **Read the job log.** Most deploy and destroy failures name their cause there. Open the job from
 **Jobs**, or run `alethia jobs logs --latest`.
- **Read the CLI's exit code.** It names the class of failure. See [Exit codes](/agents/cli#exit-codes).
- **Check the limits.** A refusal that names a number is often a ceiling. See [Limits](/reference/limits).

If nothing here helps, open a case from **Support** in the console, with the job ID and the exact
message.

records.title: MCP
records.text: MCP. Fix an MCP client that cannot connect to the Alethia MCP server, or that is refused after sign-in.

records.title: MCP
records.text:
Find what your client shows, then do what the block says. How to connect a client is in
[Connect an MCP client](/guides/assistant/mcp).

records.title: MCP
records.heading: 503 "MCP is not configured on this deployment"
records.text:
**Cause:** a self-hosted console whose `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` is not an absolute `https` URL. The server
needs one to name itself in tokens.

**Fix:** set `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` to the console's `https://` address and restart the console.

records.title: MCP
records.heading: An error during sign-in that names the client
records.text:
**Cause:** the client cannot identify itself with a Client ID Metadata Document. The server does not
accept anonymous dynamic client registration.

**Fix:** update the client to a version that supports Client ID Metadata Documents.

records.title: MCP
records.heading: 403 after sign-in
records.text:
**Cause:** one of three things, and the response says which: AI is turned off for the organization, an
owner turned agent access off, or the token carries no scope the server reads.

**Fix:** ask an owner to turn AI or agent access back on, or connect again and approve at least `read`.

records.title: MCP
records.heading: 403 insufficient_scope on a connection that used to work
records.text:
**Cause:** the connection was made before Alethia added agent scopes. It holds only `openid`, `profile`
and `email`.

**Fix:** disconnect the Alethia MCP server in the client, connect it again, and approve the scopes the
consent page asks for: `read`, `design`, `plan`, `apply`, `destroy`.

records.title: MCP
records.heading: The first request after sign-in is refused
records.text:
**Cause:** the client speaks a 2025 revision of the MCP protocol. The server accepts only the current
generation.

**Fix:** update the client.

records.title: Sign-in
records.text: Sign-in. Fix sign-in codes that do not arrive, expire, or are refused, sign-up refusals, and `alethia login` failures.

records.title: Sign-in
records.heading: Sign-in codes in the console
records.text:
The email path sends a 6-digit code. The code is valid for 10 minutes. For how the flow works, see
[Email OTP flow](/concepts/authentication#email-otp-flow).

records.title: Sign-in
records.heading: "That code didn’t work — try again."
records.text:
**Cause:** the code you entered does not match the one that was sent.

**Fix:** check the code in the most recent email and enter it again.

records.title: Sign-in
records.heading: "That code has expired. Use Resend code to get a new one."
records.text:
**Cause:** more than 10 minutes passed between sending the code and entering it.

**Fix:** select **Resend code**, and enter the new code within 10 minutes.

records.title: Sign-in
records.heading: "Too many wrong tries — that code no longer works. Use Resend code to get a new one."
records.text:
**Cause:** a code accepts only a few wrong entries. After that, it stops working.

**Fix:** select **Resend code**, and enter the new code.

records.title: Sign-in
records.heading: "Too many attempts — wait a minute, then try again."
records.text:
**Cause:** your network sent more than 5 requests to send or check a code in one minute.

**Fix:** wait 60 seconds, then try again. The **Resend code** button also waits longer after each
resend. It shows **Resend in** with a countdown.

records.title: Sign-in
records.heading: "We couldn’t send the code — try again."
records.text:
**Cause:** the email service refused or failed to send the code.

**Fix:** wait a moment and try again. If it keeps failing, sign in with GitHub, Google, GitLab, or
Bitbucket instead. On a self-hosted console, check the email settings in
[Email](/self-host/email).

records.title: Sign-in
records.heading: The form asks you to sign up instead of showing a code screen
records.text:
**Cause:** no account exists for that email address. Alethia sends an email that points to sign-up
instead of a code.

**Fix:** select **Create an account**, or use the address you signed up with.

records.title: Sign-in
records.heading: The code never arrives on a self-hosted console
records.text:
**Cause:** when a self-hosted console has no email provider set, it does not send email. It writes
the code to the server log instead, on a line that starts with `[email] no provider configured`.

**Fix:** read the code from the console's log, or set up an email provider. See
[Email](/self-host/email).

records.title: Sign-in
records.heading: "Too many accounts were created from your network today. Try again tomorrow, or ask a teammate to invite you."
records.text:
**Cause:** the network you are on reached the daily ceiling for new accounts. The ceiling is listed
in [Limits](/reference/limits).

**Fix:** try again after 00:00 UTC, or ask someone in an existing organization to invite you.
Existing accounts can still sign in.

records.title: Sign-in
records.heading: "Use a permanent email address to create an account. Temporary inbox services aren’t accepted."
records.text:
**Cause:** the address belongs to a temporary inbox service.

**Fix:** sign up with an address you keep, or with GitHub, Google, GitLab, or Bitbucket.

records.title: Sign-in
records.heading: "The security check couldn’t load. Allow challenges.cloudflare.com, or sign in with a provider above."
records.text:
**Cause:** the console shows a security check, and a browser extension, a firewall, or a network
filter blocked it.

**Fix:** allow `challenges.cloudflare.com`, or sign in with one of the providers. If you see
"Complete the security check, then try again.", finish the check and submit again.

records.title: Sign-in
records.heading: Messages after a provider sign-in
records.text:
Message What to do 
 --- --- 
 "We couldn’t sign you in with that provider — try again." Try again. If it repeats, use another provider or the email path. 
 "Sign-in was cancelled." You closed or refused the provider's screen. Start again. 
 "Your session expired — please sign in again." Sign in again. 
 "Single sign-on isn’t set up for that organization." Ask your organization's administrator. 
 "Single sign-on is temporarily unavailable — try again shortly." Wait, then try again.

records.title: Sign-in
records.heading: alethia login
records.text:
`alethia login` opens a browser page where you approve the sign-in. The code it shows is valid for 10
minutes. For the full flow, see [Login](/reference/cli/authentication#login).

records.title: Sign-in
records.heading: "this login code has expired or was already used — run alethia login again"
records.text:
**Cause:** the code is older than 10 minutes, or it was already approved.

**Fix:** run `alethia login` again, and approve the new code in the browser.

records.title: Sign-in
records.heading: "timed out after 10m0s waiting for the login to be approved in the browser"
records.text:
**Cause:** nobody approved the code in the browser. This is common on a machine without a browser.

**Fix:** run `alethia login --no-browser`. The CLI prints the URL and the code, and you open the URL
on any device.

records.title: Sign-in
records.heading: "The sign-in was refused in the browser. Nothing was shared and no token was issued"
records.text:
**Cause:** someone selected the refuse option on the browser page.

**Fix:** if you started the login, run `alethia login` again and approve it. If you did not, see
[Refusing a login you did not start](/reference/cli/authentication#refusing-a-login-you-did-not-start).

records.title: Sign-in
records.heading: "ALETHIA_TOKEN is set, and every command uses it ahead of a stored sign-in"
records.text:
**Cause:** the `ALETHIA_TOKEN` environment variable, or the `--token` flag, is set. A token always
wins over a stored sign-in, so signing in would change nothing.

**Fix:** unset `ALETHIA_TOKEN`, then run `alethia login`. To see which credential the CLI uses, run
`alethia auth status`.

records.title: Sign-in
records.heading: "authentication required. Please run alethia login"
records.text:
**Cause:** this machine has no stored sign-in, or the sign-in ended.

**Fix:** run `alethia login`.

records.title: Sign-in
records.heading: "failed to connect to server"
records.text:
**Cause:** the CLI cannot reach the control plane.

**Fix:** check your network. If you use a self-hosted console, check the control plane URL with
`alethia login --web-origin `.

records.title: Tutorials
records.text: Tutorials. Learn Alethia by building something real, start to finish, on a cloud you own.

records.title: Tutorials
records.text:
A tutorial is a lesson with one path: it tells you what to type and ends with something running.
For a specific task, use the [guides](/guides). For why the product works as it does, read the
[concepts](/concepts). If a step does not give the result the page promises, the page has a bug:
please report it.

records.title: Tutorials
records.heading: Available tutorials
records.text:
**[Deploy Online Boutique to three environments](/tutorials/online-boutique)**: build one cluster
that hosts three environments at three isolation levels, and deliver a twelve-service shop into two
of them. About 40 minutes, most of it waiting for the cluster. Tested on Hetzner Cloud, AWS, and
Google Cloud.

**[Start from a template](/tutorials/start-from-a-template)**: copy two of the public starter
templates. Connect one as a cluster's ArgoCD apps repository and the other as a bring-your-own Helm
chart, and watch both sync. About 30 minutes, most of it waiting for the cluster. Tested on Hetzner
Cloud.

records.title: Tutorials
records.heading: Before you begin
records.text:
- [Install the CLI](/get-started/install-the-cli) and run `alethia login`.
- Have an account on a supported cloud, with permission to create clusters and networks.

 
 Tutorials **create real infrastructure that costs money.** Each one ends with a teardown step, and
 you are not finished until you run it.

records.title: Deploy Online Boutique to three environments
records.text: Deploy Online Boutique to three environments. Build one Kubernetes cluster with three environments at three isolation levels, and deliver a twelve-service shop into two of them — all from the terminal.

records.title: Deploy Online Boutique to three environments
records.text:
In this tutorial you build **one Kubernetes cluster** that hosts **three environments**. Two of them
run their own copy of Online Boutique, a twelve-service shop, delivered by ArgoCD. You do it all
from the terminal, with one file and one command.

The second and third environments cost no new cluster and no new network: they are placed onto the
cluster the first one owns. It takes about 40 minutes, most of it waiting for the cluster.

 
 This tutorial creates **real infrastructure that costs money** while it runs. The last step tears
 it down. You are not finished until you run it.

records.title: Deploy Online Boutique to three environments
records.heading: What you build
records.text:
P["prod · dedicated owns the Fabric"]
 F --> D["dev-1 · namespace namespace boutique-dev-1"]
 F --> S["staging · vcluster its own Kubernetes API server"]
 D --> DA["overlays/dev-1 12 services"]
 S --> SA["overlays/staging 12 services, 2 frontends"]
`} />

A **Fabric** is the infrastructure: the cluster, its network, and its DNS. An **environment** is
placed onto a Fabric, and its **placement** sets how isolated it is:

 Placement What the environment gets 
 --- --- 
 `dedicated` Its own Fabric. This is the placement that creates a cluster. 
 `namespace` A namespace on a cluster that already exists. 
 `vcluster` Its own Kubernetes API server, running inside a cluster that already exists. 

In this tutorial, `prod` owns the Fabric and runs no application. `dev-1` and `staging` are placed
onto it, and each one deploys an overlay of the shop from the public
[alethia-examples](https://github.com/alethialabs-io/alethia-examples) repository. For the model
behind this, see [Fabrics and placement](/concepts/fabrics-and-placement).

records.title: Deploy Online Boutique to three environments
records.heading: Before you begin
records.text:
You need:

- The `alethia` CLI, [installed](/get-started/install-the-cli) and signed in with `alethia login`.
- An account on Hetzner Cloud, AWS, or Google Cloud, with permission to create a cluster and a
 network.
- A runner to execute the jobs. Check with:

 alethia runner list
 
 If no runner is online, [register one you run yourself](/guides/runners/self-operated).

This tutorial is tested on Hetzner Cloud, AWS, and Google Cloud. If you only want to learn the
product, use **Hetzner**. It is the cheapest, and you connect it with one token.

records.title: Deploy Online Boutique to three environments
records.heading: Step 1 — Connect your cloud account
records.text:
In the Hetzner Cloud Console, create a **new project** for this tutorial. In that project, go to
 **Security → API tokens** and generate a token with **Read & Write** access.

 Then connect it. The command asks for the token and hides what you type:

 alethia connector hetzner
 
 A Hetzner token can do anything inside its project, so the project is the only boundary you get.
 That is why you use a new, empty one. Hetzner has no keyless option, because it has no OIDC
 provider. See [Connect Hetzner](/guides/connectors/hetzner).
 
 
 With the `aws` CLI signed in to the account you want to use, run:

 alethia connector aws
 
 This deploys a CloudFormation stack. The stack creates an IAM OIDC provider that trusts Alethia,
 and a role that Alethia assumes. No access keys are created. See [Connect AWS](/guides/connectors/aws).
 
 
 Alethia cannot turn on Google Cloud APIs for you. Turn on the two that this tutorial needs. Use
 your own project ID in place of `my-gcp-project`:

 gcloud services enable container.googleapis.com cloudkms.googleapis.com --project my-gcp-project
 
 Then connect the project:

 alethia connector gcp --project my-gcp-project
 
 This creates a service account and

records.title: Deploy Online Boutique to three environments
records.heading: Step 2 — Describe the project in one file
records.text:
Create a file named `alethia.yaml`. It declares the project, its three environments, the size of the
cluster, and which overlay each environment deploys. Replace `my-account` with the value from the
**Account** column.

 
 
 yaml title="alethia.yaml"
 project: boutique
 cloud:
 account: my-account
 region: nbg1
 environments:
 - name: prod
 stage: production
 placement: dedicated
 components:
 cluster:
 instance_types: [cpx32]
 node_min_size: 3
 node_desired_size: 3
 node_max_size: 3
 - name: dev-1
 stage: development
 placement: namespace
 namespace: boutique-dev-1
 components:
 repositories:
 apps_destination_repo: https://github.com/alethialabs-io/alethia-examples
 apps_path: examples/online-boutique/overlays/dev-1
 - name: staging
 stage: staging
 placement: vcluster
 namespace: boutique-staging
 components:
 repositories:
 apps_destination_repo: https://github.com/alethialabs-io/alethia-examples
 apps_path: examples/online-boutique/overlays/staging
 
 Three `cpx32` nodes have 4 vCPU and 8 GB each, at about €35 a month per node. You can also use
 the region `fsn1` or `hel1`.
 
 
 yaml title="alethia.yaml"
 project: boutique
 cloud:
 account: my-account
 region: us-east-1
 envir

records.title: Deploy Online Boutique to three environments
records.heading: Step 3 — Preview what will be created
records.text:
alethia plan

This compares the file with what already exists in your organization. It lists the project, the
three environments, and their components. It changes nothing and starts no job.

records.title: Deploy Online Boutique to three environments
records.heading: Step 4 — Apply it
records.text:
alethia apply

The CLI shows the same plan and asks you to confirm. Then it deploys each environment in the order
the file lists them, and waits for each one:

1. `prod` creates the network and the cluster, then installs ArgoCD and the platform add-ons.
2. `dev-1` creates its namespace on that cluster and deploys its overlay.
3. `staging` creates its vcluster on that cluster and deploys its overlay.

The `prod` deploy runs an OpenTofu plan and then a **verify gate** before it builds anything. The
gate refuses the deploy if the plan breaks a control, for example a database open to the internet.
Its verdict is a signed receipt. See [the verification gate](/concepts/elench).

To watch the current job from a second terminal:

alethia jobs logs --latest --follow

When every environment is deployed, the CLI prints `boutique is up.`

records.title: Deploy Online Boutique to three environments
records.heading: Step 5 — Check the result
records.text:
List the environments:

alethia project env list --project boutique

You see three environments in one project.

Look at the cluster:

alethia cluster get boutique

The **GitOps** row counts the ArgoCD Applications on the cluster, and how many are synced and
healthy. If a deploy failed, the row names the step that failed instead.

Check the signed receipt from the deploy that built the cluster:

alethia verify receipt --project boutique

A list of jobs opens. Select the `prod` deploy. The command checks the receipt's signature against a
key the control plane trusts, and exits with a non-zero status if the check fails. You can use the
same command to gate a CI pipeline. See [`alethia verify`](/reference/cli/verify).

 
 To use `kubectl`, run `alethia cluster kubeconfig boutique`. See
 [Get a kubeconfig](/guides/get-a-kubeconfig).

records.title: Deploy Online Boutique to three environments
records.heading: Step 6 — Add a fourth environment
records.text:
Run this:

alethia cluster list

There is **one** cluster. Three environments run on it. Each has its own application and its own
namespace, and `staging` also has its own Kubernetes API server.

To add another environment, add another entry to `alethia.yaml`. The repository has a `dev-2`
overlay that uses the namespace `boutique-dev-2`:

 - name: dev-2
 stage: development
 placement: namespace
 namespace: boutique-dev-2
 components:
 repositories:
 apps_destination_repo: https://github.com/alethialabs-io/alethia-examples
 apps_path: examples/online-boutique/overlays/dev-2

Then deploy only that environment:

alethia apply --env dev-2

No new cluster is created. The node sizes in Step 2 are tested with three copies of the shop
running, so `dev-2` fits. To add more environments than that, first raise `node_desired_size` and
`node_max_size` on `prod`.

records.title: Deploy Online Boutique to three environments
records.heading: Clean up
records.text:
Destroy the environments that are placed on the cluster **first**, and the environment that owns
the cluster **last**. If you add `dev-2`, destroy it first too.

alethia project destroy --project boutique --env dev-1 --yes --wait
alethia project destroy --project boutique --env staging --yes --wait
alethia project destroy --project boutique --env prod --yes --wait

 
 Do not destroy `prod` first. Destroying `prod` removes the cluster, and Alethia does not stop
 you while other environments are still placed on it. After that, the other environments can no
 longer be torn down cleanly, and the cloud identities created for their namespaces can be left
 behind.
 

Then make sure nothing is left. Your cloud provider's console has the final answer. Load balancers,
volumes, and NAT gateways are the resources that most often survive a failed teardown, and they bill
by the hour.

 
 
 hcloud server list
 hcloud load-balancer list
 hcloud volume list
 hcloud network list
 
 
 Every resource Alethia creates on AWS carries the tag `Application=alethia`:

 aws resourcegroupstaggingapi get-resources --tag-filters Key=Application,Values=alethia --region us-east-1
 aws ec2 describe-nat-gateways --

records.title: Deploy Online Boutique to three environments
records.heading: What you did
records.text:
You:

- Built one Fabric that carries environments at three isolation levels.
- Delivered a different version of the same application to two environments, through GitOps.
- Had the deploy that built the cluster checked by a signed verify receipt, which you checked
 yourself.
- Did all of it from a terminal, so you can also do it from CI.

Next, read about [promoting changes between environments](/concepts/promotions) and
[drift detection](/concepts/drift).

records.title: Start from a template
records.text: Start from a template. Copy two of Alethia's public starter templates, deploy one as the ArgoCD apps repository of a Hetzner cluster and the other as a bring-your-own Helm chart, and watch both sync.

records.title: Start from a template
records.text:
In this tutorial you copy two of Alethia's public starter templates and put both on **one Kubernetes
cluster** on Hetzner Cloud:

- [alethia-starter-apps](https://github.com/alethialabs-io/alethia-starter-apps) becomes the
 cluster's **ArgoCD apps repository**. ArgoCD syncs a small application from it into three
 namespaces.
- [alethia-starter-chart](https://github.com/alethialabs-io/alethia-starter-chart) becomes a
 **bring-your-own Helm chart**. Alethia installs it as an add-on, in a namespace of its own.

This is the setup the templates' own deploy test runs on Hetzner. You build it from the terminal,
with one file and a few commands, in about 30 minutes, most of it waiting for the cluster.

 
 This tutorial creates **real infrastructure that costs money** while it runs. The last step tears
 it down. You are not finished until you run it.

records.title: Start from a template
records.heading: What you build
records.text:
1 control plane + 2 cpx32 workers"]
 C --> A["ArgoCD apps repository your copy of alethia-starter-apps"]
 C --> B["Bring-your-own chart your copy of alethia-starter-chart"]
 A --> A1["apps · namespace starter"]
 A --> A2["apps-dev · namespace starter-dev"]
 A --> A3["apps-staging · namespace starter-staging"]
 A --> A4["addons · nothing yet"]
 B --> B1["addon-starter-chart · namespace starter-chart"]
`} />

The two templates run under two different trust levels. The apps repository can create any kind of
resource on its cluster. A bring-your-own chart can create only a closed list of namespaced
workload kinds in its own namespace, and no RBAC. For the full comparison, see [Starter Templates](/guides/design-project/starter-templates).

records.title: Start from a template
records.heading: Before you begin
records.text:
You need:

- The `alethia` CLI, [installed](/get-started/install-the-cli) and signed in with `alethia login`.
- A Hetzner Cloud account.
- A GitHub account, to hold your copies of the two templates.
- A runner to execute the jobs. Check with:

 alethia runner list
 
 If no runner is online, [register one you run yourself](/guides/runners/self-operated).

records.title: Start from a template
records.heading: Step 1 — Copy the two templates
records.text:
A template is a starting point, not a dependency. You make your own copy, and Alethia deploys your
copy. Nothing in either template reports back to Alethia.

1. Open [alethia-starter-apps](https://github.com/alethialabs-io/alethia-starter-apps) on GitHub.
2. Select **Use this template**, then **Create a new repository**.
3. Name it `my-starter-apps`, and set it to **Public**.
4. Do the same for [alethia-starter-chart](https://github.com/alethialabs-io/alethia-starter-chart),
 and name the copy `my-starter-chart`.

Use **public** copies for this tutorial. ArgoCD clones a public repository anonymously, so you do not
have to connect GitHub to Alethia first. That is also how the tested run cloned them. To use a
private copy, first connect GitHub as a [Git provider](/guides/connectors/git-providers).

In the rest of this tutorial, replace `my-github-account` with your GitHub user or organization name.

records.title: Start from a template
records.heading: Step 2 — Connect Hetzner
records.text:
In the Hetzner Cloud Console, create a **new project** for this tutorial. In that project, go to
**Security → API tokens** and generate a token with **Read & Write** access.

Then connect it. The command asks for the token and hides what you type:

alethia connector hetzner

A Hetzner token can do anything inside its project, so the project is the only boundary you get.
That is why you use a new, empty one. See [Connect Hetzner](/guides/connectors/hetzner).

Now find the name of the account you connected:

alethia connector list

Note the value in the **Account** column. You use it in the next step.

records.title: Start from a template
records.heading: Step 3 — Describe the project in one file
records.text:
Create a file named `alethia.yaml`. Replace `my-account` with the value from the **Account** column,
and `my-github-account` with your GitHub name.

yaml title="alethia.yaml"
project: starter
cloud:
 account: my-account
 region: nbg1
environments:
 - name: dev
 stage: development
 placement: dedicated
 components:
 cluster:
 instance_types: [cpx32]
 node_min_size: 2
 node_desired_size: 2
 node_max_size: 2
 repositories:
 apps_destination_repo: https://github.com/my-github-account/my-starter-apps

Three things in this file matter:

- **`placement: dedicated` gives the environment its own cluster.** The overlay discovery in
 Step 5 runs only on a dedicated cluster. The template also creates its own `Namespace` objects,
 which a namespace placement refuses.
- **`apps_destination_repo` is your copy of alethia-starter-apps.** It is the repository ArgoCD syncs.
- **There is no `apps_path`.** With no overlay path, ArgoCD syncs the repository root, and it also
 turns each directory under `overlays/` into an Application of its own. If you set a path, that
 discovery stops. See [Repositories](/guides/design-project/repositories).

The cluster is the size the templates are tested on: one cont

records.title: Start from a template
records.heading: Step 4 — Preview and deploy
records.text:
Preview what the file creates:

alethia plan

This lists the project, its environment and its components. It changes nothing and starts no job.

Now deploy:

alethia apply

The CLI shows the same plan and asks you to confirm. Then it creates the network and the cluster,
installs ArgoCD and the platform add-ons, and connects ArgoCD to your apps repository. To watch the
job from a second terminal:

alethia jobs logs --latest --follow

When the deploy is done, the CLI prints `starter is up.`

records.title: Start from a template
records.heading: Step 5 — Check that the apps repository synced
records.text:
alethia cluster get starter

The **GitOps** row counts the ArgoCD Applications on the cluster, and how many are synced and
healthy. Every Application should be both.

Four of those Applications come from your copy of alethia-starter-apps:

 Application Synced from Namespace What it runs 
 --- --- --- --- 
 `apps` the repository root `starter` one `hello` Deployment and its Service 
 `apps-dev` `overlays/dev` `starter-dev` the same, with 1 replica 
 `apps-staging` `overlays/staging` `starter-staging` the same, with 2 replicas 
 `addons` `addons/` none nothing yet. It is still Synced and Healthy 

You did not declare `apps-dev` or `apps-staging` anywhere. ArgoCD found the two directories under
`overlays/` and made one Application for each. To get a third, add `overlays/prod` to your copy and
push it. No Alethia deploy is needed.

 
 Every Application from the apps repository syncs automatically, prunes, and self-heals. A commit
 to the default branch of your copy deploys on its own, so **write access to that branch is deploy
 access to the cluster.**

records.title: Start from a template
records.heading: Step 6 — Attach the chart template
records.text:
Attach your copy of alethia-starter-chart to the `dev` environment as a bring-your-own chart:

alethia chart attach starter-chart --project starter --env dev --repo https://github.com/my-github-account/my-starter-chart --chart-path chart --ref HEAD --namespace starter-chart

Each flag maps to one field of the chart:

 Flag Value Why 
 --- --- --- 
 `starter-chart` the chart's ID Its ArgoCD Application is named `addon-starter-chart` 
 `--chart-path` `chart` The directory in the repository that holds `Chart.yaml` 
 `--ref` `HEAD` The default branch. Use a tag if you want each release to be explicit 
 `--namespace` `starter-chart` Alethia creates this namespace, and the chart may create resources only in it 

Attaching a chart also queues a **safety scan**. The runner renders the chart in an isolated sandbox
and checks what it would create. Follow the scan with:

alethia jobs logs --latest --follow

 
 Bring-your-own charts are an opt-in feature of each Alethia instance. If `alethia chart attach`
 says they are not enabled, ask the operator of your instance.

records.title: Start from a template
records.heading: Step 7 — Deploy again
records.text:
The chart is attached, but nothing has installed it yet. Run the same command as before:

alethia apply

The file has not changed, so the plan shows no new resources. The deploy still runs, and this time
it renders the chart's ArgoCD Application. It reuses the cluster from Step 4 and creates no new
server.

records.title: Start from a template
records.heading: Step 8 — Check that the chart synced
records.text:
List the charts attached to the environment:

alethia chart list --project starter --env dev

The **Scan** column shows the result of the safety scan. Then look at the cluster again:

alethia cluster get starter

The **GitOps** row now counts one more Application, `addon-starter-chart`, and it is synced and
healthy. It manages three resources in the `starter-chart` namespace: a Deployment, a Service and a
ConfigMap. None of them is cluster-scoped and none of them is RBAC, which is the contract every
bring-your-own chart must meet.

A bring-your-own chart syncs differently from the apps repository:

- **Prune is off.** A resource you delete from the chart keeps running until you delete it yourself.
- **Self-heal is off.** A change made by hand stays, and the Application reports `OutOfSync`. That
 is information, not an error.

Before you change your chart, run the template's own contract check against it. Run it from a
clone of your copy, with `helm` installed:

hack/check-byo-contract.sh chart

It fails if the chart renders a kind that a bring-your-own chart cannot create.

records.title: Start from a template
records.heading: Clean up
records.text:
alethia project destroy --project starter --env dev --yes --wait

This removes the cluster, its network and everything ArgoCD installed on it. Your two GitHub
repositories stay. They are yours.

Then make sure nothing is left. The Hetzner Cloud Console has the final answer. Servers, load
balancers and volumes bill by the hour, and they are the resources that most often survive a failed
teardown.

hcloud server list
hcloud load-balancer list
hcloud volume list
hcloud network list

records.title: Start from a template
records.heading: What you did
records.text:
You:

- Copied two templates, and deployed your copies rather than the originals.
- Connected one as the ArgoCD apps repository of a dedicated cluster, and saw overlay discovery
 turn two directories into two Applications.
- Attached the other as a bring-your-own chart, which runs in its own namespace under a
 default-deny project.
- Did it all from a terminal, so you can also do it from CI.

The third template, [alethia-starter-ai](https://github.com/alethialabs-io/alethia-starter-ai), uses
both trust levels at once. Read [Starter Templates](/guides/design-project/starter-templates) to see
where it puts each component and why. For the model behind the apps repository, read
[GitOps & ArgoCD](/concepts/gitops-argocd).
